schema_ddl:
CREATE TABLE PRODUCT (
    PRODUCT_ID INT,
    PRODUCT_NAME VARCHAR(255),
    UNIT_PRICE INT,
    PRIMARY KEY (PRODUCT_ID),
    CHECK (UNIT_PRICE > 0)
);

CREATE TABLE SALES (
    PRODUCT_ID INT,
    SELLER_ID INT,
    BUYER_ID INT,
    SALE_DATE DATE,
    QUANTITY INT,
    PRICE INT,
    FOREIGN KEY (PRODUCT_ID) REFERENCES PRODUCT(PRODUCT_ID),
    CHECK (QUANTITY > 0),
    CHECK (PRICE > 0)
);
q1: SELECT P.PRODUCT_ID, P.PRODUCT_NAME FROM PRODUCT P INNER JOIN ( SELECT PRODUCT_ID FROM SALES GROUP BY PRODUCT_ID HAVING MIN(SALE_DATE) >= '2019-01-01' AND MAX(SALE_DATE) <= '2019-03-31' ) S ON (P.PRODUCT_ID = S.PRODUCT_ID)
q2: SELECT PRODUCT_ID , PRODUCT_NAME FROM PRODUCT WHERE PRODUCT_ID NOT IN (SELECT CASE WHEN SALE_DATE NOT BETWEEN '2019-01-01' AND '2019-03-31' THEN PRODUCT_ID ELSE 0 END NEW FROM SALES)
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT P.PRODUCT_ID, P.PRODUCT_NAME FROM PRODUCT P INNER JOIN ( SELECT PRODUCT_ID FROM SALES GROUP BY PRODUCT_ID HAVING MIN(SALE_DATE) >= '2019-01-01' AND MAX(SALE_DATE) <= '2019-03-31' ) S ON (P.PRODUCT_ID = S.PRODUCT_ID)
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT PRODUCT_ID , PRODUCT_NAME FROM PRODUCT WHERE PRODUCT_ID NOT IN (SELECT CASE WHEN SALE_DATE NOT BETWEEN '2019-01-01' AND '2019-03-31' THEN PRODUCT_ID ELSE 0 END NEW FROM SALES)
explanation: Q1 retrieves products whose all sales occurred strictly within the date range '2019-01-01' to '2019-03-31'. Q2 retrieves products whose at least one sale occurred outside that date range. They are complements of each other, not equivalent.
counterexample_dsp: A product with sales on '2018-12-31' and '2019-02-15'. Q1 excludes it (not fully within range), Q2 includes it (has a sale outside range).
